formation.explanation: Leader proposals acquire current term/index and enter the unstable log. Self and follower append acknowledgments wait for caller persistence before contributing Match support. Voting membership selects the majority order statistic (both majorities in joint mode); maybeCommit additionally requires the selected entry to have the current leader term. Append broadcasts propagate new commit, while heartbeats cap it by each follower Match. Followers check the previous entry and prevent committed-prefix overwrite. Ready exposes committed entries in order; snapshot and application quota can delay delivery. Caller application and Advance or async responses update application bookkeeping.

context.explanation: A promotable node without unapplied committed configuration changes can campaign. Pre-vote does not change term; real candidacy increments term and persists votes, and only current voting quorum support wins. Winning leadership resets follower progress, appends an empty entry and begins replication. Step normally relinquishes authority on higher term and rejects old replies; pre-vote and lease exceptions are explicit. Same-term leader messages displace candidates. CheckQuorum can step down. Transfer suppresses proposals until a caught-up voter receives TimeoutNow, with timeout abort and normal election safeguards. Removal can optionally step down the leader.

connection.explanation: Membership qualifies both election and replication support. Term resets discard old match/vote/readOnly acknowledgment tracking; Step rejects stale responses, while previously committed history remains binding. Entry stability acknowledgments retain the producing term to avoid discarding a replaced unstable suffix; old snapshot completions remain meaningful because snapshots carry committed state. Restart loads durable history/configuration and enters follower state. Pending pre-commit reads live separately from the reset readOnly queue and are released on response-based current-term commit. Applied membership may reinterpret existing matches and produce a commit without that same read-release callback. Application completion can propose automatic joint exit, but transfer admission can reject that proposal. Timeout abort clears the transfer field without rescheduling this action; subsequent applied entries or snapshot completion reevaluate it. Whether an application-free periodic suffix remains closed is a local continuation question.

grounding.derivation: ConfChangeTransitionJointImplicit specifies automatic exit by a zero configuration proposal; ConfState.AutoLeave and tracker.Config explicitly assign this transition to Raft when possible, contrasting explicit mode where the application must propose it. The application already proposed and applied the entering configuration. appliedTo implements the internal continuation and explicitly anticipates rejection during transfer and a later retry. This establishes implementation ownership beyond the word automatic alone. Under retained leadership and a viable joint quorum after transfer abort, absence of an unrelated client command must not permanently eliminate that continuation. Generic caller retry duties for external proposals do not require inventing new client work to drive an already applied automatic transition. No numeric deadline is claimed; only a closed repeating execution without an internally driven transition would witness the requirement gap.
grounding.applicability: Committed implicit joint change applied in order; transfer overlaps its application acknowledgment and later aborts; eligible leader retained, viable incoming/outgoing quorums, reliable ongoing ordinary message delivery and ticks, storage/application work completed; no crash or new client commands.
unresolved: Fixed recurrence observations and semantic correspondence have not yet been executed/reviewed.
alternatives: A later committed application callback legitimately retries and may recover; a new leader may generate such progress with its empty entry. These do not promise an event in the stable-leader, application-free suffix.
